mainTopic: מנחות done שלא לשמן: valid but not counting for the owner, the exceptions of מנחת חוטא and מנחת קנאות, and why further deviation is forbidden
overview: מסכת מנחות opens with a general rule. If a כהן removes the handful (קמיצה) from a מנחה while thinking of a different kind of מנחה (שלא לשמן), the offering is still כשרה, but the owner has not fulfilled his obligation. There are two exceptions, מנחת חוטא and מנחת קנאות. These become פסולות if any of the four main services is done שלא לשמן, even with mixed intentions in either order. The גמרא asks why the משנה says "אלא" ("but") instead of a simple "and". It answers that only the owner loses out: the מנחה itself stays כשרה, so it is forbidden to keep deviating in its remaining services. This matches רבא's ruling that after an עולה was slaughtered שלא לשמה, its blood may still not be sprinkled שלא לשמה. The גמרא supports this with a סברא: one deviation does not permit more. It also brings a פסוק, "מוצא שפתיך", which calls the offering both a נדר and a נדבה. This teaches that an offering not brought as vowed still stands as a valid נדבה.

steps.title: Meal offerings done for the wrong purpose are still valid
steps.stepSummary: The משנה states the general rule: a מנחה whose handful was removed שלא לשמן is כשרה, but it does not count toward the owner's obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: All meal offerings from which the handful was removed not for their own sake are valid, but they do not count for the owner as fulfilling his obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens the מסכת with a basic rule about a מנחה that was handled with the wrong intention.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule has two parts. First, the offering itself stays כשרה, so the service continues as usual. Second, the owner gets no credit for his obligation, so he still has to bring another מנחה.

keyTerms.meaning: Meal offerings, made of flour, brought in the בית המקדש
The handful was removed. This is the קְמִיצָה, the כהן scooping a fistful of the flour to burn on the מזבח
Not for their own sake, meaning with the intention of a different type of offering
Valid; the offering may continue to be brought
They did not count for the owners as fulfilling their obligation

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up "כשרות" with "the owner is יוצא". The offering is valid and is still brought, yet the owner must bring a new one to fulfill his obligation.
steps.whyThisMatters: This two-part rule (valid offering, no credit for the owner) is the base of the whole first פרק, and the גמרא's very first question is about how it is worded.

phrases.english: MISHNA: All the meal offerings
from which a handful was removed not for their sake are valid,
phrases.notes: "Not for their sake" means the כהן was thinking of a different kind of מנחה while scooping.

phrases.english: but they did not count for the owners
as fulfilling the obligation,

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מנחה whose קמיצה was done שלא לשמן is כשרה, but the owner has not fulfilled his obligation.

steps.title: Two meal offerings are excluded from the rule
steps.stepSummary: The משנה names two exceptions to the general rule: מנחת חוטא and מנחת קנאות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Except for the meal offering of a sinner and the meal offering of jealousy.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה limits its general rule by naming two meal offerings that do not follow it. The next line will spell out what happens to them instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For these two offerings, the "still valid" part of the rule does not apply. This line only names the exceptions; the details of their פסול come in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Except for
The meal offering of a sinner, brought by a very poor person for certain sins in place of an animal or birds
The meal offering of jealousy, brought as part of the סוטה process

phrases.english: except for the meal offering of a sinner and the meal offering of jealousy.
phrases.notes: The "meal offering of jealousy" is the one brought for a סוטה, a woman her husband suspects of being unfaithful.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the general rule of step 1 by naming two exceptions
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מנחת חוטא and מנחת קנאות do not follow the general rule of remaining כשרות when done שלא לשמן.

steps.title: How the two exceptions become disqualified
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a מנחת חוטא or מנחת קנאות becomes פסולה if any of the four main services is done שלא לשמן, or even with mixed intentions.
steps.simpleTranslation: A meal offering of a sinner or a meal offering of jealousy whose handful was removed not for its sake, or whose handful was placed in a vessel, carried to the altar, or burned not for its sake, or for its sake and not for its sake, or not for its sake and for its sake, is disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains what happens with the two exceptions: wrong intention makes them פסולות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Four services are listed: removing the handful, putting it in a כלי, carrying it to the מזבח, and burning it. A wrong intention at any one of them disqualifies these offerings. Even a mix of right and wrong intention, in either order, disqualifies them.

keyTerms.meaning: Disqualified; the offering may not be brought
He placed the handful into a כְּלִי שָׁרֵת, a holy service vessel
He walked; carrying the handful to the מזבח (the הוֹלָכָה)
He burned the handful on the מזבח (the הַקְטָרָה)
For their sake and not for their sake, meaning mixed intentions

phrases.english: A meal offering of a sinner and a meal offering of jealousy
from which he removed the handful not for their sake,

phrases.aramaic: נָתַן בִּכְלִי וְהָלַךְ וְהִקְטִיר שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָן,
phrases.english: or he placed it in a vessel, or carried it, or burned it not for their sake,
or for their sake and not for their sake,
or not for their sake and for their sake, they are disqualified.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִנְחַת חוֹטֵא וּמִנְחַת קְנָאוֹת שֶׁקְּמָצָן שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the law for the exceptions named in step 2
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מנחת חוטא and מנחת קנאות are פסולות if any of the four services is done שלא לשמן, or with mixed intentions in either order.

steps.title: What mixed intentions means
steps.stepSummary: The משנה defines both orders of mixed intention using the example of מנחת חוטא and מנחת נדבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: How is it for their sake and not for their sake? For the sake of a meal offering of a sinner and for the sake of a voluntary meal offering. Not for their sake and for their sake? For the sake of a voluntary meal offering and for the sake of a meal offering of a sinner.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains the term "mixed intentions" from the last step by giving examples.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first case the correct intention (חוטא) comes first and the wrong one (נדבה) second. In the second case the order is flipped. Either way, the offering is פסולה.

keyTerms.meaning: How? Introduces an explanation
A voluntary meal offering, brought by choice and not because of any obligation

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's rule: most מנחות stay כשרות when done שלא לשמן, but the owner gets no credit. מנחת חוטא and מנחת קנאות become פסולות from any wrong intention, even mixed with the right one, in any order.

phrases.english: How is it for their sake and not for their sake?

phrases.aramaic: לְשֵׁם מִנְחַת חוֹטֵא וּלְשֵׁם מִנְחַת נְדָבָה.
phrases.english: For the sake of a meal offering of a sinner and for the sake of a voluntary meal offering.
Not for their sake and for their sake?

phrases.aramaic: לְשֵׁם מִנְחַת נְדָבָה וּלְשֵׁם מִנְחַת חוֹטֵא.
phrases.english: For the sake of a voluntary meal offering and for the sake of a meal offering of a sinner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the mixed-intention cases mentioned in step 3
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Mixed intention means intending both the correct מנחה and a different one, in either order.

steps.title: Why does the משנה say "but" instead of "and"?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה used the word "אלא" ("but") when a simple "and" would have expressed the rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Why do I need the משנה to say "but"? Let it say: "And they did not count for the owners as fulfilling the obligation!"
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by questioning one word in the משנה's first line. It is setting up a search for what the word "אלא" teaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "And" would just add a second fact: valid, and no credit. "But" sounds like a limit on the word "כשרות", hinting at something extra. The גמרא wants to know what that extra lesson is.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need? Asks why something seems unnecessary
To teach, meaning to state in the משנה
But; here it seems to limit what came before it
Let it teach, meaning the משנה should have said it this way

phrases.english: GEMARA: Why do I need it to teach "but"?
phrases.notes: He means the word אלא in the משנה's first line: "but they did not count for the owners."

phrases.aramaic: לִיתְנֵי: וְלֹא עָלוּ לַבְּעָלִים לְשֵׁם חוֹבָה!
phrases.english: Let it teach: "And they did not count for the owners as fulfilling the obligation!"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה's first line (step 1) and questions its wording
steps.kashyaTarget: The word "אלא" in the משנה's opening rule
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A plain "and" would have stated both facts, so "but" seems extra and must be teaching something.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What extra lesson does the word "אלא" teach beyond a simple "and"?

steps.title: The word 'but' teaches that the offering itself stays valid
steps.stepSummary: The word "אלא" teaches that only the owner loses out. The מנחה itself is still כשרה, so it is forbidden to keep changing its intention.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the משנה teaches us: only the owner fails to fulfill his obligation. The מנחה itself is valid, and it is forbidden to deviate again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 5. The word "אלא" is there to teach that the מנחה itself is still a real, valid offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Had the משנה said "and," we might think the offering is somewhat damaged and no longer important. "אלא" limits the problem to the owner's obligation. Because the offering stays כשרה, the rest of its services must still be done properly לשמה.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it teaches us. It explains why a word or detail is there.
The owners, meaning the person who brought the offering
Counting toward his obligation
To change, meaning to do a service with a different intention than the offering's own

steps.confusionAlert: "Not counting for the owner" does NOT mean the offering is פסולה. It is fully כשרה and is still brought on the מזבח. It just does not fulfill the owner's obligation.

phrases.english: This is what it teaches us:

phrases.aramaic: לַבְּעָלִים הוּא דְּלֹא עָלוּ לְשׁוּם חוֹבָה,
phrases.english: it is only for the owner that they did not count toward the obligation,
but the meal offering itself is valid,
and it is forbidden to deviate,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 5 about the word "אלא".
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the משנה says "אלא" instead of "and".
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: "אלא" teaches that only the owner's obligation is lost. The מנחה stays כשרה, so further deviation is forbidden.

steps.title: This matches רבא's ruling about a burnt offering
steps.stepSummary: The rule fits רבא's statement: if an עולה was slaughtered שלא לשמה, its blood may still not be sprinkled שלא לשמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like רבא, who said: if someone slaughtered an עולה not for its own sake, it is forbidden to sprinkle its blood not for its own sake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the rule it just learned from "אלא" matches a known ruling of רבא about animal offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's case has the same structure. One service, the slaughtering, was already done with the wrong intention, yet the next service must still be done properly. The same is true for a מנחה: after a wrong קמיצה, the later services must still be לשמה.

keyTerms.meaning: A burnt offering, which is burned completely on the מזבח
Slaughtering the animal
Sprinkling or throwing the blood on the מזבח

steps.whyThisMatters: It sets a general principle for all קרבנות: one mistake does not give permission for further mistakes.

phrases.english: This is like רבא, as רבא said:
a burnt offering that one slaughtered not for its own sake,
it is forbidden to sprinkle its blood not for its own sake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Connects the rule in Step 6 to a parallel ruling of רבא.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that you may not keep deviating after one service was done שלא לשמן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא's ruling about an עולה slaughtered שלא לשמה.

steps.title: A logical reason: one mistake does not permit more
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers two possible supports for רבא's rule. The first is a סברא: just because you deviated once, should you keep deviating in everything?
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, use logic; if you want, use a פסוק. Logic: just because he deviated once, should he go ahead and deviate in all the rest?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא announces that it will give two supports for רבא's rule, a reason and a פסוק. It then gives the reason first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is common sense. One wrong action was done, but that does not "break" the offering so that anything goes from then on. Each later service still has to be done properly.

keyTerms.meaning: If you wish, say. It introduces one of several possible answers or supports.
A logical argument
A פסוק, a verse

phrases.aramaic: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא סְבָרָא, וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא קְרָא.
phrases.english: If you wish, say a logical argument; and if you wish, say a verse.
If you wish, say a logical argument:
Because he deviated with it once,
should he go on and deviate with it in all these?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא סְבָרָא, וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first of two supports for רבא's rule.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's rule that you may not keep deviating.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Logic: one deviation does not justify further deviations.

steps.title: A verse support: "what comes out of your lips"
steps.stepSummary: The second support is a פסוק in דברים about keeping your vows. It mentions both נדר and נדבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you wish, use a פסוק: "What comes out of your lips you shall keep and do, as you vowed to ה' your God, a נדבה."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the פסוק that will be its proof. This step only quotes the פסוק; the next steps will analyze its wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is not yet clear here. The key detail is that the פסוק starts by speaking of a vow, נדרת, but ends with the word נדבה. The גמרא is setting up a question about that.

keyTerms.meaning: What comes out of your lips, meaning what you said or promised
A vowed offering. You obligate yourself ("I take upon myself an offering"), so you are responsible to bring it.
A gift offering. You designate a specific item, with no ongoing obligation.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say a verse:
"What comes out of your lips you shall keep and do,
as you have vowed to the Lord your God, a gift offering",

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second, scriptural support promised in Step 8.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's rule that, once one service was done שלא לשמה, the remaining services may not also be done שלא לשמה.

steps.title: Is it a vow or a gift?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out a problem in the פסוק: it calls the same offering a נדר and then a נדבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A נדבה? It is a נדר! The פסוק calls it a נדר and also calls it a נדבה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices a contradiction inside the פסוק. This difficulty will become the key to the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נדר and נדבה are two different kinds of offerings. The פסוק says "as you vowed," so why does it end with "נדבה"? The extra word must be teaching something.

keyTerms.meaning: It calls it

steps.confusionAlert: This question is not attacking the earlier ruling. The גמרא is pointing out an odd word in the פסוק so it can learn the lesson from it.

phrases.english: A gift offering? It is a vow offering!

phrases.aramaic: קָרֵי לֵיהּ נֶדֶר וְקָרֵי לֵיהּ נְדָבָה!
phrases.english: It calls it a vow and it calls it a gift offering!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the wording of the פסוק quoted in Step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording of the פסוק, which uses both נדר and נדבה for one offering.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One offering cannot be both a נדר and a נדבה, so the double wording seems contradictory.

steps.title: If not done as vowed, it becomes a gift offering
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק teaches that an offering brought as vowed fulfills the נדר. If not, it still counts as a valid נדבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if you did as you vowed, it is a נדר. If not, it is a נדבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the double wording. The פסוק is describing two outcomes for one offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An offering brought שלא לשמה does not fulfill the owner's vow, but it does not become worthless. It is still a holy offering, a נדבה. That is exactly the משנה's rule: valid, but not counting for the owner's obligation. Since it is still a real offering, it must be treated properly, so further deviation is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It introduces the correct understanding.
It will be

steps.whatToRemember: Most מנחות and other קרבנות brought שלא לשמה are still כשרות (a נדבה), but the owner has not fulfilled his obligation. The exceptions, like מנחת חוטא and מנחת קנאות, become פסולות. Because a valid offering is still a real offering, one may not keep deviating in its remaining services (רבא). This is supported by סברא and by the פסוק "מוצא שפתיך".
steps.whyThisMatters: In this סוגיא the פסוק backs up רבא's rule. An offering not brought as vowed still stands as a holy נדבה, which is why its remaining services must still be done properly. This matches the משנה's picture: the offering is valid, but the owner gets no credit.

phrases.english: Rather, if you acted according to how you vowed,
it will be a vow offering,
and if not, it will be a gift offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the difficulty raised in Step 10 and completes the proof from the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the double wording as two possible outcomes
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק seems to call one offering by two contradictory names.
steps.terutzMaskana: Done as vowed, it is a נדר. Done differently, it is still a valid נדבה that does not fulfill the vow.
